title: Mata Sundari
hook: after Guru Gobind Singh, she guided the Sikhs through letters and counsel
tomorrow: Mata Sahib Kaur, mother of the Khalsa

segments.voice: Yesterday, Mata Jito, and the sweets dropped into the iron bowl beside the blade. Your line: sweetness in the steel.

A sheet of paper, folded and sealed. A rider carries it out of Delhi, along dusty roads, to a village where Sikhs are waiting for word. Someone opens it and reads it aloud to the whole room: blessings, counsel, requests, in the name of a woman. The Guru who led them in person is gone. The community is scattered and under pressure. And for a stretch of years, tradition says, a great deal of what held them together arrived like this: in letters, from a widow in Delhi. Today: Mata Sundari.
screen: `A SEALED LETTER LEAVES DELHI.` → `READ ALOUD TO THE SANGAT.` → `SIGNED BY A WOMAN.`

segments.voice: Mata Sundari was a wife of Guru Gobind Singh, and tradition remembers her as the mother of his son Ajit Singh, who fell at Chamkaur. When the Guru left Anandpur and the hard years came, she and Mata Sahib Kaur went to Delhi. Later the Guru traveled south, and he died there. Tradition says he named no person to follow him as Guru: the Guruship would rest in the scripture and in the Khalsa. So who would the Sikhs turn to with a question, a quarrel, a need? Tradition says they turned to Mata Sundari. She led through hukamnamas, letters of instruction and blessing. The Gurus had sent them before her, to congregations far away. Now letters went out in her name, tradition says, to sangats across the Punjab and beyond: asking them to keep the Sikh way, to support the community's needs, to stay united, and blessing them. Sikhs remember her settling disputes and sending trusted Sikhs to care for holy places. Notice what kind of leading this was. No army. No throne. She didn't claim to be the Guru, and the tradition doesn't say she was. She led by being trusted, by writing, by counsel, by staying faithful to what the Guru had set up and asking others to stay faithful too. It fits this whole week. Mata Nanaki, who waited in faith. Bibi Viro, joy amid trouble. Mata Gujri, steady to the end. Kirpa Ram, who came back to serve. Pir Budhu Shah's sacrifice. Mata Jito's sweetness in the steel. And now Mata Sundari, holding a scattered people together with ink and patience.
screen: `A WIFE OF GURU GOBIND SINGH.` · `NO PERSON AFTER HIM AS GURU.` · `LETTERS OF COUNSEL AND BLESSING.` · `LEADING BY BEING TRUSTED.` · then, large: `SHE LED.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who could use a few lines from you right now: a younger cousin, a friend starting something new, a coworker who's struggling. Let the breath slow, and find what you'd want them to hear: one piece of counsel, one blessing. Keep it short, the way a letter read aloud should be.
Mata Sundari. A wife of Guru Gobind Singh who, after his death, guided the Sikhs from Delhi through letters and counsel. Today's word.
Your line: she led. No throne, just ink and trust. That's the end of a week.
